scores.evidence: “Both protocols can be valid.” For nested evaluation, it specifies “Tune hyperparameters exclusively within each outer training partition, using inner folds” and requires that “Outer-fold outcomes must not inform later choices among methods, settings, or procedures.”
“Using unlabeled evaluation inputs is not inherently leakage” explicitly distinguishes input access from labels: “Keep target labels accessible only to the evaluator for scoring.”

“Confirmatory if the adaptation procedure is fixed beforehand” permits prespecified adaptation. It requires defining target-input access and limits the estimand: “Results support performance of the specified adaptation procedure on the evaluated target setting.”

“target-label metrics must not guide adaptation settings, checkpoint selection, or later procedural choices” identifies label-based leakage. It also states: “The design alone cannot establish performance on unseen target domains.”

“Both protocols can be valid” expressly accepts nested evaluation with “Refit using that outer training partition, then evaluate once on its held-out outer fold.” Its restrictions concern evaluation feedback and training boundaries, rather than rejecting rotation of data roles across folds.
